title: Singapore wealth fund, Saudi Telecom bid for UK’s Pure Data Centres stake — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 16): Singaporean wealth fund GIC Pte and Saudi Telecom Co are among the final bidders competing for a stake in data centre developer Pure Data Centres Group, people with knowledge of the matter said.

GIC has teamed up with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners for its offer for UK-based Pure DC ahead of a deadline for binding bids later this month, according to the people.

Pure DC’s owner Oaktree Capital Management is seeking to bring in a new minority investor to help bankroll an expansion of the business, which develops and operates digital infrastructure underpinning artificial intelligence.

Oaktree could seek a valuation of around US$8 billion ($10.3 billion) for Pure DC in any stake sale, one of the people said, asking not to be identified discussing confidential information. Bloomberg News reported last year that Oaktree was seeking to raise funds for Pure DC.

Deliberations are ongoing and there’s no certainty that any of the suitors will decide to bid for a stake in Pure DC, the people said.

“Pure is growing quickly and we’re always looking for partners who can help us take advantage of the opportunities ahead of us,” a spokesperson for Pure DC said in an emailed statement. They declined to comment on valuation.

See also: Malaysian data centre loan syndication delayed in rare deal pause

Representatives for CIP, GIC, Oaktree and Saudi Telecom declined to comment.

Pure DC has been positioning itself as a means for the UK, Europe and the Middle East to catch up on the AI-fuelled data centre boom, with developers already pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into projects in places like the US and China.

The company has more than one gigawatt of capacity live or under development, its website shows. Pure DC this month secured up to US$1.9 billion in debt financing to help pay for a build-out across Europe and the Middle East.

title: Vujcic says bets on ECB hike in 2027 don’t seem unreasonable
article:
(Nov 16): Market wagers on the European Central Bank (ECB) tightening monetary policy in 2027 may prove accurate, Vice President Boris Vujcic said, becoming one of the first officials to discuss moves beyond an expected hike next month.

Reiterating that there’s no pre-determined path for borrowing costs, the Croatian official said the current inflation outlook warrants a continued measured response, suggesting interest rates will rise further following two increases since the Iran war began.

“Pricing of another rate hike next year does not seem unreasonable from where we stand at the moment,” Vujcic said on Monday in Frankfurt. “But there’s much to happen between now and then.”

Inflation is currently running at twice the ECB’s 2% target, while the economy is holding up well in the face of multiple headwinds. Investors are currently betting on two quarter-point increases in the deposit rate in 2027, following one in December. Most analysts surveyed by Bloomberg, however, don’t see the ECB moving beyond next month.

Vujcic’s comments echo Lithuanian central bank governor Gediminas Simkus, who told Econostream Media that rates may have to be lifted further in 2027.

See also: Thai GDP growth rebounds as AI drives investments, exports

“I’m not sure that December’s hike alone would be enough,” the Lithuanian official said in an interview published on Monday. “Further tightening next year might be necessary, depending on the inflation outlook and strength of policy transmission.”

title: Korea’s instant ramen giants take their spicy rivalry global
article:
(Nov 16): For nearly four decades, NongShim Co has dominated South Korea’s instant-noodle market with its signature Shin Ramyun. But when Korean ramen became a global phenomenon, it was a rival that captured the world’s appetite — and investors’ imagination.

Samyang Foods Co did it with its Buldak, which became a viral sensation with global fans filming themselves eating the intensely spicy noodles on social media. The craze pushed Samyang’s overseas sales above 80% of revenue — compared with NongShim’s 37% — and lifted its market value to nearly four times that of its rival.

Now NongShim is spending heavily to rebuild investor confidence.

At the heart of the push is a 200 billion won factory for NongShim’s iconic Shin Ramyun in the port city of Busan, the company’s first dedicated export plant and home to what the company calls the world’s fastest instant-noodle production lines. The facility will boost NongShim’s domestic export capacity by 70% as it seeks to regain ground lost to Samyang overseas.

“We may have been somewhat slow in responding to global demand early on because our products were so deeply loved at home for so long,” said Songha Ji, NongShim’s head of global marketing.

A decades-old domestic rivalry between two of South Korea’s biggest food makers is intensifying overseas. NongShim and Samyang, both based in Seoul, are racing to capitalise on a K-food boom that has pushed Korean noodles into mainstream supermarkets from the US to Europe, just as the global instant-noodle market is projected to grow about 23% to US$63.3 billion by 2030.

See also: Coca-Cola raises guidance, buoyed by soda sales abroad

NongShim’s new six-story complex, which opened in October, is designed to produce 600 packets a minute on each line — twice the speed of conventional setups. Inside, raw dough takes barely seven minutes to become a shelf-ready packet of Shin Ramyun. Guided by artificial intelligence sensors and automated mixers, the noodles are rolled, flash-fried and boxed at blinding speed.

The factory will nearly double NongShim’s annual domestic export capacity to 1.2 billion packets and raise its total global capacity to 6.2 billion across Korea and four factories in the US and China. Production from Busan will initially be directed to Japan, Europe, Australia, India and Southeast Asia.

NongShim aims to double global noodle sales to 5.4 trillion won by 2030, which would lift overseas sales to more than 60% of revenue. Such growth would also elevate it to the global top five instant noodle makers alongside Nissin Foods Holdings Co and Maggi-maker Nestlé SA.

See also: Starbucks says it’s not buying Chipotle, dousing deal rumours

NongShim’s push puts it head-to-head with Samyang. The Buldak maker is rapidly gaining ground in overseas markets where NongShim dominated, having already overtaken it in key markets like China and Europe. It is on track to become the third-largest instant noodle seller in the US this year — right behind NongShim, according to Euromonitor International.

Samyang is also accelerating its global expansion and announced last week it would invest more than 131 billion won in a new Vietnamese production line. Its first overseas plant in China is set to open in January.

For NongShim, the test will be whether the new capacity translates into faster sales growth and improved profitability. The company’s valuation could get a lift from a rebound in US sales and increased output from the Busan facility, according to Hanwha Investment & Securities analyst Han Yujung.

NongShim’s push for overseas growth has a promising early start — sales of Shin Ramyun abroad jumped 36% in the first half of this year.

Still, Samyang commands a valuation premium over NongShim, its stock is trading at 13.4 times forward earnings versus the latter’s 11.4 — meaning investors are paying more per won of projected profit in anticipation of faster growth.

NongShim is also borrowing from its rival’s playbook. To court Gen Z shoppers abroad, it has leaned into pop culture — launching limited-edition Shin Ramyun tied to Netflix’s K-Pop Demon Hunters, partnering with K-pop group aespa as global ambassadors and setting up booths at fan conventions globally.

On Monday, Nongshim unveiled a limited seafood edition of Shin Ramyun, co-developed with celebrity chef Edward Lee, to mark the 40th anniversary of the flagship noodle brand. It also plans to roll out a new stir-fried Shin Ramyun next year, entering the soupless-noodle category that propelled Buldak’s global success.

“We cannot yet claim that we are outperforming Samyang in many international markets,” Ji, NongShim’s marketing head, said. “But we are studying and benchmarking what Samyang has done well.”

title: US diesel falls below US$6 a gallon, easing key inflationary pressure
article:
(Nov 16): US retail diesel prices dropped below US$6 a gallon for the first time since early September, taking some pressure off a key inflationary input that has pushed the price of energy and food higher this fall.

Retail diesel prices dropped to US$5.9989 a gallon on Monday (Nov 16), according to AAA, down from a peak over US$6.50 a gallon in late September.

Diesel supplies have been squeezed tighter than most other fuels since the US-Iran war began, choking off energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz for months. And while crude oil cargoes have recovered, fuel remains curtailed. That shortage has since been exacerbated by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, pushing the country — in normal times the world’s second-largest exporter of diesel — to curb diesel shipments through the end of January.

The resulting price spike has squeezed farmers, truck drivers and everyday consumers in the US and around the world. Diesel is often referred to as the “workhorse fuel of the global economy” for its role in powering tractor-trailers hauling food to grocery stores, farm equipment, home heating and even backup electricity generators at data centres. The economy-wide impacts of higher diesel prices can be seen in wholesale inflation that’s risen at the fastest pace since 2022.

The White House worked to rein in diesel costs ahead of this fall’s midterm elections, with a range of measures from loosening restrictions around a tax-free dyed variant of the fuel to attempting to import diesel from Russia. The efforts, at least electorally, proved largely unsuccessful, with Republicans suffering historic losses.

To be sure, prices have come down meaningfully and fleet-wide supply agreements often allow truckers to pay less for fuel than the listed retail price. Meanwhile, heating oil futures settled Friday near US$4.26 a gallon — well off the highest prices this year.

See also: European gas dips as record US flows counter storage concerns

But that’s the highest seasonal price ever recorded. The retail price, similarly, is still above the highest price ever recorded before 2026.

title: Burnham set to say Brexit has not worked
article:
(Nov 16): UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will tell an audience in London’s financial district on Monday that Brexit has not worked and a new deal must be sought, starting at a summit with the European Union (EU) later this week.

The prime minister will follow convention by giving a speech about foreign policy at the Lord Mayor’s banquet. He will argue that the world has changed since the EU referendum of 2016, meaning that the UK should have a closer relationship with its neighbouring democracies.

“The Brexit we were given has not worked,” Burnham is expected to say, according to pre-briefed remarks. “We have lost more than we gained.”

The speech kicks off a crucial week for two of the government’s most politically sensitive policies. On Tuesday, Alan Milburn — a former Labour minister who served under Tony Blair — will publish a report on Britain’s youth unemployment crisis. Burnham’s government has pledged to get more young people into work and eventually reduce the country’s huge welfare costs.

“Benefits must become the backstop, not the starting point,” the Labour leader wrote in an opinion article in the Guardian newspaper on Sunday.

Also over the weekend, Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said young people who have been unemployed for a year would be guaranteed work under an expanded government programme. Ministers are expected to reveal more details of Labour’s plan to boost job opportunities following publication of Milburn’s report.

See also: UK's Burnham tries to hush down his own talk of rejoining EU

Then, on Friday, UK officials arrive in Brussels for a delayed summit with the EU. Burnham is pursuing a new deal that targets a modest number of areas including trade barriers on agrifood products, a youth mobility programme and linking of emissions trading systems.

Speaking to broadcasters ahead of the speech on Monday morning, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the Brexit deal had hurt trade with the EU, and Burnham is seeking to fix that.

People voted for Brexit “primarily because they wanted positive economic change”, Miliband said on Sky News. “Unfortunately we have had the opposite.”

See also: Asda’s flat sales end losing streak as new CEO joins UK grocer

In his speech at the Lord Mayor’s banquet, Burnham is expected to acknowledge that some sectors have adapted to Brexit — a possible nod to the financial sector. However, he will argue that businesses as a whole are worse off, as are consumers.

The British Chambers of Commerce (BCC), a lobby group, urged Burnham to come back with a deal that reduces the cost of trade, adding that the current arrangements — sealed by former prime minister Boris Johnson — are “still failing to deliver, almost six years after Brexit”.

In a statement on Sunday night, the BCC said “businesses face customs, VAT (value-added tax), regulatory and mobility barriers, alongside rising protectionism, global subsidies and the EU’s emerging ‘Made in Europe’ agenda”. Over half of exporters want EU customs paperwork and delays at the border to be removed, a BCC survey showed.

title: Malaysian data centre loan syndication delayed in rare deal pause
article:
(Nov 16): A US$488 million ($628.8 million) loan for a Malaysian data centre project backed by private equity firm Actis has been delayed while being marketed to other lenders, according to people familiar with the matter.

A planned online presentation scheduled for Nov 2 by loan arrangers for other banks invited to participate in the financing by Epoch Digital Pte Ltd didn’t take place, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private information. A visit planned for the same week to the data centre, whose computing capacity will be used by TikTok owner ByteDance Ltd, also failed to happen.

Lead arrangers HSBC Holdings Plc, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp and Bank of China have signed the loan and committed to providing Epoch Digital with the funds, according to the people. But the missed online presentation and site visit are important and standard steps for prospective banks that need to undertake due diligence on the loan before deciding to participate in syndication, and mark a rare postponement.

Management of Epoch Digital wasn’t available on the scheduled dates, prompting the delay in the syndication timeline, said one of the people.

A representative for London-based Actis declined to comment, while Epoch Digital didn’t respond to a request for comment. Spokespeople for HSBC and SMBC declined to comment, while representatives from AIIB and Bank of China didn’t immediately respond.

The delay points to the complexities around financing the AI buildout as a growing number of new players rush to meet the demand for computing capacity, while lenders juggle the flood of borrowing requests against internal exposure limits. PricewaterhouseCoopers estimates spending on data centres could reach US$8.2 trillion in the Asia-Pacific by 2050, though the facilities globally face growing pushback from citizens concerned about their societal impact.

See also: Nvidia’s CEO search draws fire with Bessent’s ‘shake-up’ call

The online presentation and site visit are being coordinated for new dates, said the people.

Owned almost totally by Actis-managed funds, Epoch Digital was established in November 2022 and its first data centre development was in Taiwan, details on Actis’ website show.

Arrangers had reserved the right to amend the syndication timetable at any time, according to the people. Banks syndicating loans in Asia typically like to keep deals moving smoothly along timetables laid out in invitations to other lenders.

title: US, partners agree to safeguard key AI tech, infrastructure
article:
(Nov 16): The US and nine partner nations including India, Singapore and the UK signed a pledge to safeguard sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure amid escalating strategic competition with China over the future of artificial intelligence (AI).

The “San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity” establishes a framework for the protection of critical goods, software, knowledge materials, and components essential to AI supply chains.

The pact targets those items “whose theft, illicit transfer, or acquisition by hostile actors would confer a meaningful military or intelligence advantage”, the US State Department said in a statement.

The joint actions comes amid an urgent reassessment in Washington over how to control the exports and use of top-tier accelerators by China. The debate has been sparked by revelations that Nvidia Corp’s chief Jensen Huang had an affair with a former data centre executive whom the US suspects is a Chinese spy.

It also comes days before US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

Part of the broader US-led “Pax Silica” initiative, the agreement also covers vital physical and digital infrastructure including ports, transport systems, communications and logistics networks, “whose disruption, degradation, hostile control, or the unauthorised exposure of the data flowing through them would cause significant harm or dysfunction”.

See also: Post-Jensen US chip curbs threaten Southeast Asia’s AI boom

The declaration underscores Washington’s broader push to institutionalise allied economic security architecture as competition with China over frontier technologies intensifies. The other signatories are Australia, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

Asked about the development during a regular press briefing on Monday, China Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokeswoman Mao Ning said “we should not draw ideological lines or form exclusive cliques” when it comes to AI. “Parties should join hands in promoting development and governance of AI and make it serve the common well-being of humanity”.

Asked if Xi and Trump would discuss they issue when they meet later this week, she said “both sides are in communication in this regard”.

See also: Why compute will be the next big AI trade

South Korea’s Second Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Kim Jina attended a Pax Silica retreat hosted by the US Department of State in San Francisco on Sunday and signed the agreement, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday. Kim discussed ways for “like-minded nations to cooperate in building a trustworthy AI ecosystem”.

Japan’s Foreign Ministry also confirmed that the government signed the economic-security focused declaration on Sunday with like-minded nations, as part of initiatives under Pax Silica.

The US State Department said participating governments plan to establish joint working groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, AI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation, safe harbours and supply chain security hubs, and AI security and resilience.

They also pledged coordinated efforts to address economic coercion and supply chain disruptions, while seeking to protect private investment and ensure “a level playing field for innovation and growth”.

Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden are also expected to sign the declaration in the coming days, according to the Financial Times, which reported the agreement earlier.

title: China’s economy disappoints with stimulus yet to lift investment
article:
(Nov 16): China’s growth weakened across the board in October as investment unexpectedly worsened while consumption and industrial output undershot estimates, in a sign Beijing’s latest stimulus measures have yet to feed through to the economy.

Retail sales rose just 0.4% from a year ago, a sharp slowdown from September and far below the consensus forecast of 0.8% by economists polled by Bloomberg. Industrial output expanded at a slower rate for the first time in three months and grew 4.8% in October.

Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in the first 10 months of 2026 from the same period last year, lower than the 7% decline expected by economists. For the single month of October, investment contracted 17% from 2025, according to Bloomberg Economics, its sharpest fall outside the Covid-19 pandemic.

“We are still in the waiting period for the stimulus impact to kick in,” said Helen Qiao, the chief economist for Greater China at BofA Global Research. Policymakers “are probably expecting things to get worse from here in 2027 and 2028, and there’s a willingness to hold back some of the stimulus,” she told Bloomberg TV.

The figures revealed an economy that’s again at risk of losing momentum, even after Beijing stepped up efforts to bolster growth in late September. What especially stood out was the sharp deterioration in investment, a key lever long used by officials to stimulate growth during downturns.

See also: China car output slows to four-year low as domestic demand drops

Economists had expected the investment decline to narrow, after the government rolled out greater public borrowing quota and accelerated spending on major construction projects via a 800 billion-yuan (US$120 billion or $154 billion) programme. That makes a deepening fall in capital expenditure on infrastructure all the more perplexing.

There’s a rising concern that a confluence of political and economic factors is crippling the once-powerful tool.

An ongoing leadership reshuffle of the Communist Party — which will culminate in a major congress next year — could make cadres more cautious about committing to projects, a sentiment likely fanned by the raging anti-corruption campaign.

See also: Due diligence for China directors

In addition, a mid-2027 deadline to eliminate local government financing vehicles — platforms that carried “hidden” or off-balance-sheet debt amassed by authorities in the provinces — likely also distracted officials from new projects as they scrambled to clean up the old borrowing.

Any major economic reforms will likely be deferred until after the Communist Party holds its 2027 congress and ushers in the next generation of decision makers, according to Carlos Casanova, a senior economist for Asia at Union Bancaire Privee.

Coupled with the anti-corruption campaign, “this could contribute to policy paralysis and weigh on economic growth in the fourth quarter of 2026 and 2027”, he said.

In a sign Beijing has ample fiscal dry powder, government deposits at banks in October increased substantially more than what normal seasonal patterns would imply, suggesting the funds raised in the fourth quarter may only be used in early 2027 to support growth, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc economists. Public spending fell for the seventh straight month in September.

Other details in Monday’s report point to the widening divergence in the economy. While electronics manufacturing output surged nearly 20% in October from a year ago thanks to the global boom in artificial intelligence investment, car production slowed sharply and climbed just 0.9%, the worst reading since the end of Covid. Intense competition and falling sales mean carmakers are headed for another year of record low profit margins.

As domestic demand weakens, retail sales are on track to finish the year with the weakest growth since the pandemic. Their performance isn’t much different even if cars are excluded.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Residential prices continued to fall in October, extending a slump that’s dragged on economic growth for more than five years. Property investment plunged 21.6% in the first 10 months of the year from a year earlier, compared with a 20.6% decline in January-September.

The statistics agency described the state of the economy as “overall stable” and said it had “extended a trend of renewing growth engines and improving its structure”, In a statement, the National Bureau of Statistics highlighted challenges faced by the economy include an uncertain global environment, imbalances between supply and demand, as well as difficulties in some businesses’ operations.

Despite indications that growth has come under pressure, the urban surveyed jobless rate unexpectedly slipped to 5.1% last month from 5.2% in September. Many economists see the official unemployment measure as an incomplete reflection of the labour market because it excludes migrant workers who returned to the countryside after losing work.

The economy rebounded in the third quarter, with growth reaching the lower end of Beijing’s annual target of 4.5% to 5%. But the recovery remained heavily reliant on overseas demand, with net exports contributing almost 40% of the increase in gross domestic product (GDP) — the most for any quarter since the start of 2025.

That dependence is becoming a bigger risk as questions mount over the sustainability of the global artificial intelligence investment boom, which has powered demand for Chinese electronics and other manufactured goods. A slowdown in exports would increase pressure on domestic consumption and investment to pick up the slack.

At the same time, after GDP expanded 4.6% in the first three quarters from a year ago, officials can tolerate some slowdown in the final months. The economy only needs to grow 4.3% in the last quarter for China’s full-year GDP to hit the lower bound of the official goal.

The October figures will be closely scrutinised by top officials ahead of the Central Economic Work Conference, usually held in the first half of December. The gathering will offer clues on Beijing’s economic priorities for 2027 and the scale of any additional support.

Policymakers may lean more heavily on fiscal measures if the economy loses further momentum.

The People’s Bank of China has signalled caution about cutting interest rates when borrowing demand is already weak. And in a potential sign of unease over market expectations for further easing, the central bank is draining funds from the financial system via a medium-term liquidity facility for the first time in five months.

“The Chinese authorities need to find out the reason behind the investment cliff,” said Raymond Yeung, the chief economist for Greater China at Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd. “This is an area where fiscal policy can play a significant role.”

title: YTL Power scrutinised amid Nvidia turmoil, alleged China links
article:
(Nov 16): YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR) shares took a breather Monday after their worst weekly selloff in nearly two years as turmoil surrounding Nvidia Corp and allegations the Malaysian utility has links to Chinese-connected firms cast a shadow over its artificial intelligence business.

The utility firm’s shares plunged 13% last week, the steepest weekly decline since January 2025, erasing more than RM3 billion (US$733 million) in market value. Intensifying scrutiny over Nvidia following Jensen Huang’s ouster as chief executive over reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy, has weighed on YTL.

Adding to concerns, spy-themed short seller Culper Research alleged in a May report that Megaspeed International — the Singapore-based cloud firm at the centre of the Nvidia controversy — is a major YTL customer. Citing a Megaspeed employee, Culper claimed YTL sought to keep the relationship private as it supplied Nvidia chips to Chinese customers including Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.

YTL and Megaspeed haven’t publicly confirmed such a relationship, and Culper’s claims haven’t been independently verified.

YTL Power and parent YTL Corp Bhd (KL:YTL) didn’t respond to requests for comment. Megaspeed didn’t respond to requests for comment.

See also: Ex-Malaysia digital star that built PM’s avatar is mired in debt

In a Monday research note, MBSB Research analyst Royce Tan said there is no credible evidence implicating YTL Power for alleged chip diversion, but added that a formal clarification from the utility would address uncertainties.

“We believe it is important to distinguish the allegations surrounding Nvidia and Megaspeed from YTL Power’s own operations, which is mainly a co-location model where it provides space, power and cooling to third-party tenants rather than directly operating GPU computing infrastructure,” Tan wrote.

See also: Johor property prices rise as demand favours homes near RTS Link

YTL Power was up about 3% Monday and is currently valued at RM39 billion. Parent YTL Corp gained 1% Monday after a 10% weekly slump last week.

YTL Power partnered with Nvidia in 2023 for a RM20 billion artificial intelligence data centre project in Malaysia, helping propel its shares to record highs. The facility in Johor state began operating in October 2025, running Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell chips.

Malaysia said it’s examining whether AI chips brought into the country by a unit of Megaspeed were subsequently shipped overseas. The trade ministry said Megaspeed unit Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia and brings in its own servers and AI chips for its operations.

Megaspeed is under scrutiny following reports that its former chief executive officer Alice Huang allegedly helped Chinese technology companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips.

title: Singapore property frenzy returns with sales hitting year-high
article:
(Nov 16): Singapore's new private home sales jumped to a one-year high in October, in a sign of continuing demand that is driving a decade-long rally in prices.

Developers sold about 1,716 units in the month, according to data released on Monday (Nov 16) by the country’s Urban Redevelopment Authority. That is the highest since the same period last year, when more than 2,400 units were sold, and compares with the 296 sold in September.

It is also a sign of the impact that so-called mega launches are having on the market. Much of the demand last month came from a single project released at the end of the month — Thomson Reserve — which sold about 90% of the 1,268 homes its developers plan to build. Some of the transactions will only be captured in November’s data.

Such projects have attracted a mix of wealthy locals and immigrants, despite curbs imposed by the city state’s government in recent years to deter speculation. In a country with some of the world’s priciest private homes, many favour property investments as a stable investment and store of wealth.

Even so, sales had been tepid in recent months with a dearth of high-profile project releases and rising local lending rates.

See also: Hongkong Land's pace of capital recycling ahead of target after selling another US$500 mil worth

“Sales activity in many existing projects remained relatively modest, indicating that demand continues to be targeted rather than broad-based,” said Leonard Tay, the head of research for property broker Knight Frank’s Singapore business. He expects new homes sales this year to reach slightly under 8,000 units, compared to 10,815 sold last year.

“Buyers are also factoring in wider economic considerations, including the possibility of higher financing costs in the near future and evolving employment prospects,” he said in a note.

title: Indonesian rupiah falls to record low as Fed bets boost dollar
article:
(Nov 16): The Indonesian rupiah fell to a fresh record low, pressured by a stronger dollar amid hawkish US Federal Reserve expectations, lingering worries over domestic political stability and a potential market downgrade.

The rupiah dropped 0.4% to 18,264 per dollar on Monday (Nov 16). The currency has weakened about 9% this year to underperform regional peers.

Investors have soured on the nation’s assets this year due to concerns over Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s policy uncertainty, the exits of several key policymakers and MSCI Inc’s warning that it could downgrade Indonesia’s equity market to standalone status. Most recently, the resignation of vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka compounded those worries, while growing bets on Fed rate hikes boosted the dollar and further pressured the rupiah.

Bank Indonesia has said that it will remain present in the markets to maintain the rupiah stability. It regularly intervened in the currency’s spot market as well as offshore and onshore non-deliverable forwards. The central bank has also been buying government bonds in the secondary market to stem volatility.

title: Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 to examine how AI and digital money reshape finance
article:
Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 will examine how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital money are changing financial services, alongside how regulatory approaches are evolving to support innovation while safeguarding financial stability.

The festival will run from Nov 18 to 20 at Singapore EXPO. Its programme will also cover shifts in trade and capital flows, financing for infrastructure and economic growth, and the implications of AI for jobs and skills.

“The decisions we make today about technology, regulation and financial infrastructure will shape how finance serves businesses and individuals for years to come,” says Kenneth Gay, chief FinTech officer at the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

MAS and the Global Finance & Technology Network (GFTN) are organising the 11th edition in collaboration with the Association of Banks in Singapore. Last year’s gathering drew more than 70,000 attendees from 142 countries and about 1,000 speakers, according to the statement.

Senior public- and private-sector leaders will meet at the invitation-only Insights2040 Annual Meetings today and tomorrow, ahead of the main festival. Their agenda includes accountability and liability in agentic systems, challenges in scaling tokenised markets, and global frameworks and shared practices for payment chains.

Those discussions will also examine sovereignty and the resilience of the financial system. The meetings will take place at Sands Expo & Convention Centre.

See also: MAS, Bank of England and Bank of Thailand complete FX settlement trial

Other topics at the main festival include tokenisation and quantum technologies, as well as the role of international cooperation in the changing financial landscape.

The exhibition will span five halls and include more than 40 international pavilions. Displays will cover AI-enabled payments and agentic commerce, as well as digital assets and cross-border payments.

Access to finance for smaller businesses is another focus. The 12th Global SME Finance Forum, held in conjunction with the festival, will bring together senior executives from more than 80 countries.

See also: Why the investment industry can’t sit out the anti-scam fight

The SME Finance Forum, which is managed by the World Bank Group, is organising that event in partnership with GFTN. Its programme includes an innovation showcase, a dedicated learning day and the annual Global SME Finance Awards.

International pavilions will seek to connect businesses, investors and technology providers across markets. An India Pavilion aims to link Indian fintech firms with Singapore’s capital and financial institutions to support access to ASEAN and global markets.

The GFTN & SEGA Go-Global Pavilion will feature 30 technology companies from Shanghai and Shenzhen, connecting them with international investors and financial institutions. SEGA stands for Smart Economy Globalisation Acceleration.

Organisers expect the festival’s SFF MeetUp programme to facilitate more than 20,000 pre-scheduled meetings, connecting attendees with potential business partners, investors and industry leaders. An Investor Hours programme will also bring together founders, general partners and limited partners to explore investment opportunities and partnerships.

title: Bitcoin options traders brace for slide to US$60,000 after selloff
article:
(Nov 16): Bitcoin options traders are bracing for further losses after last week’s bruising selloff as a tougher interest-rate outlook and a risk-off mood deepen the gloom around the cryptocurrency.

The largest concentration of put open interest on Deribit stood at the US$60,000 strike across all expiries on Monday (Nov 16), about 8% below bitcoin’s current price of around US$65,000. Puts, which give holders the right to sell at a predetermined price, are often used as protection when further drops are expected.

The positioning follows an especially sharp drop in bitcoin last week, which saw the largest digital asset fall by 12%. It hit a four-month low of nearly US$62,000 over the weekend before clawing back some of those losses. In the options market, traders remain wary.

“Market participants were looking to hedge short-term downside risk via options in very thin liquidity,” said Caroline Mauron, co-founder of Orbit Markets.

During the selloff, a gauge comparing the pricing of puts and calls expiring Friday reached 25 points in favour of puts, according to Mauron. That showed strong demand for protection against a further drop.

See also: Bitcoin slides below US$70,000 as inflation concerns hurt crypto

“The US$60,000 level has been established as a strong support, holding up twice this year as well as throughout 2024,” Mauron said. A decisive break below that level could inflict serious pain on the market, she added, with no obvious support before US$40,000.

Bitcoin briefly fell through US$60,000 on July 1, hitting a low of US$57,742 for the year but it has traded above that level since July 2.

See also: Thailand lets tourists turn crypto into baht for spending

The token’s latest swoon has come as several of the forces that once helped push it higher have reversed.

Investors have pulled almost US$3 billion from US-listed spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds since the US$6 billion Binance hack on Oct 29, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The outflows have removed a source of demand that had helped underpin the cryptocurrency.

At the same time, the outlook for US interest rates has turned more negative. Traders have added to bets on further Federal Reserve rate increases in 2027 and have begun assigning a small probability to a half-percentage-point increase in December after inflation again topped forecasts.

Crypto has also been swept up in a broader retreat from risk assets, fuelled by turmoil around the artificial-intelligence trade.

“The problem is that bitcoin is competing for attention in a crowded macro environment,” said Robin Singh, chief executive officer of Koinly. “Between the Nvidia controversy, growing economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions, investors have plenty of other things to worry about.”

That leaves bitcoin short of an obvious catalyst to draw buyers back in, according to Singh, who said the cryptocurrency could struggle to rebuild momentum.

To be sure, Jeff Ko, chief analyst at ViaBTC, said bitcoin may be nearing a turning point.

“Much of the recent decline presumably reflects capital rotating into Anthropic’s IPO as investors sold liquid assets to fund their allocations,” he said, adding the token saw a similar selloff ahead of the SpaceX IPO and then rebounded quickly.

“The drop to US$62,000 over the weekend also flushed out a large share of leveraged speculative positions,” Ko said. “I think that gives a healthier base for a recovery.”

For now, technical indicators offer little comfort.

The latest decline brought bitcoin back below its 200-day and 200-week moving averages — levels seen as key long-term indicators. That “paints a bearish picture in the short term", according to Pratik Kala, a portfolio manager at Apollo Crypto.

This leaves options traders focused on a support level that has already shown resilience twice this year, with hopes that it may pull off a third rebound.

title: Nvidia’s CEO search draws fire with Bessent’s ‘shake-up’ call
article:
(Nov 16): Pressure is mounting on Nvidia Corp days after it ousted Jensen Huang as its chief executive officer, with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urging the company to make a “dramatic” leadership shake-up and come clean about its compliance with export controls on its prized artificial intelligence (AI) chips.

Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress will be under intense scrutiny on Tuesday as the chipmaker reports quarterly results in the aftermath of Huang’s dramatic exit last week over a scandal that touched off an unprecedented crisis at the chipmaker. The company has begun its search for a successor, even as some of Huang’s allies in Silicon Valley are campaigning for his return to the top job.

Bessent sought on Sunday to close off the possibility of a Huang comeback, calling on Nvidia’s board to go outside the company for new leadership after a series of accusations that it facilitated sales of its advanced AI chips to Chinese entities. In recent days, the Treasury chief has also pointed a finger at the Commerce Department for failing to do enough to enforce US export curbs.

“This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader, that they need to go outside the company,” Bessent said in an interview on Fox News’ Sunday Morning Futures. “They need a dramatic shake-up.”

Yet hours after Bessent’s interview aired, the Financial Times reported that Huang has been discussing the idea of returning to the company he co-founded more than three decades ago, with some Silicon Valley supporters putting together a “war room” to gather support. Nvidia and a Huang spokesperson declined to comment.

Nvidia’s shares were little changed in early trading on Robinhood, after a perpetual futures contract on the Hyperliquid blockchain referencing the US company’s stock price rose more than 3% Sunday. The shares are coming off their worst week since April 2025.

See also: India to benefit from unwinding of AI trade, top official says

Revelations that Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International whom the US suspects of being a Chinese spy, have forced a reckoning for the company that’s played a critical role in driving the AI boom. The former Nvidia chief evangelised AI adoption and enlisted US President Donald Trump as an ally to clear the path of regulations that could stymie growth of the technology.

The Trump administration plans to name Nvidia as one of more than two dozen AI “national champions” soon, part of ongoing efforts to help those American firms win business overseas, The Wall Street Journal reported. Washington has been formulating that list for months and could make an announcement as early as over the next week, the Journal reported, citing people familiar with the plans. Other firms to be named include Amazon.com Inc, Microsoft Corp, OpenAI and Anthropic PBC, it added, representing some of the industry’s biggest names. The designation, which stems from a 2025 executive order to promote American technology abroad, helps fast-track licensing approvals and win government financing, among other benefits, the Journal reported.

In the wake of Jensen Huang’s resignation, Bessent said he wants to know whether Nvidia intentionally ignored warning signs of shell companies, many of them in Singapore, funnelling chips to China, signalling he wants to shift the focus from the departed CEO’s personal “foibles” to the legal and national-security aspects.

See also: Alibaba unveils new flagship AI model in riposte to US rivals

“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said. “And I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel.”

The US Justice Department is spearheading an investigation into Megaspeed over suspected semiconductor smuggling and is also probing whether entities linked to Alice Huang were involved in efforts to smuggle products made by Super Micro Computer Inc to China, Bloomberg News has reported. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, and Super Micro has said Megaspeed was never one of its customers.

Nvidia’s board has launched an internal inquiry into its former CEO’s relationship with Alice Huang, though it has also said that it doesn’t believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Federal law enforcement authorities have an espionage investigation underway, along with the probes of possible chip smuggling, while key committees in Congress are kicking off their own reviews.

Huang has agreed to testify before House lawmakers behind closed doors on his relationship with Alice Huang, according to Republican Representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. His panel and two others are still sorting a date with Huang, and members are eager to understand whether any sensitive information may have been exposed, Moolenaar said on CBS’ Face the Nation.

Nvidia’s efforts to intervene in inquiries risk also drawing scrutiny from US lawmakers. The company appealed to Taiwanese officials after prosecutors on the island accused an Nvidia employee of helping to smuggle AI chips into China, Bloomberg News has reported. Nvidia raised its concerns to political officials about the manager’s July arrest, Bloomberg reported.

The case in Taiwan is separate from the investigation by US authorities into possible export control breaches by Megaspeed. In late summer 2025, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter called the head of a Commerce Department bureau that enforces export curbs to ask whether the agency had played a role in the detention of Alice Huang by Singapore authorities, Bloomberg News has reported.

Moolenaar, along with the heads of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs panels, have also asked Teter to appear next month to answer questions about the company’s adherence to export controls and news reports about what the lawmakers characterised as the company’s “interference in US export controls policies and investigations”.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Nvidia has said in response to the Bloomberg reporting on Teter’s call that it regularly consults with government officials to answer questions and provide information.

The Commerce Department’s handling of export controls has drawn attention from Congress but also from within the administration. Last Friday, Bessent said that he had long supported putting Megaspeed on a trade blacklist, but pointedly singled out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as the Cabinet official who would have to take action, and he reiterated that point on Sunday.

“As I said, many other departments were pushing for this, and Commerce had the pen,” the Treasury chief said.

Moolenaar said there also “need to be questions answered by Howard Lutnick and the entire Commerce Department”. Democrats, who officially take majority control of the House and Senate in January, are also eager to hear from Lutnick.

“It looks like he has been the barrier inside the government to stopping the flow of these Nvidia chips to China,” Representative Jim Himes of Connecticut, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence panel, said on CBS’ Face the Nation. “It is the Commerce secretary’s job and the president’s job to stop that from happening.”

A spokesperson for Lutnick told NBC News last week that he had agreed to testify before Congress.

Meanwhile at Nvidia, the board has begun its search for candidates to replace Huang, though the effort remains in early stages. First, the company must get through its quarterly report on Tuesday, which promises to be one of the most closely watched in recent memory.

A key question will be how executives on the call address the succession issue. While Nvidia shares fell 12.7% last week, some high-profile shareholders have expressed support for Huang, including his possible return to the chipmaker he turned into one of the world’s most valuable companies.

In a social media post, Altimeter Capital Management and Atreides Management cited “the extraordinary success of Jensen Huang’s leadership over a long period of time” and the uncertainty created by his departure in urging the board to take a “slow, measured, and deliberate” approach to Nvidia’s future leadership.

That should include “the potential return of Jensen Huang”, Altimeter’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides’ Gavin Baker wrote in a letter to Nvidia’s board posted on X. SpaceX and Tesla Inc CEO Elon Musk, another Huang ally, has also voiced his support for a comeback, signing an online petition.

Yet Bessent’s demands for significant change at the company and the circumstances of Huang’s departure make the odds of his return small. Moolenaar, whose committee focuses on China’s strategic rivalry with the US, suggested the ousted CEO should have known that “every Chinese national” can be pressured to spy by the Communist Party.

“That was simply irresponsible and a direct threat to our national security,” he said.

title: China car output slows to four-year low as domestic demand drops
article:
(Nov 16): China’s car production stalled in October as a prolonged slump in domestic demand intensifies overcapacity pressures in the world’s biggest auto market.

Production grew just 0.9% in October from a year earlier, according to government data. That’s the slowest since 2022, when China’s strict Covid Zero policies led to widespread manufacturing disruptions.

China’s market has been plagued by production overcapacity as the removal of subsidies and an economic slowdown hurt consumer demand, leaving manufacturers with too many cars and chasing too few buyers. An export boom has helped ease some of that pressure, but growing protectionism in key overseas markets risks chipping away at that buffer.

Earlier this month, China’s Passenger Car Association warned that exports will slow to a 10% growth rate in 2027 due to the introduction of tariffs or import quotas in overseas markets.

title: US colleges see further declines in international student enrollment
article:
(Nov 16): US universities are seeing continued declines in international enrolment with an estimated 15% drop in new foreign students this fall, according to a subset of data from the Institute of International Education.

The total number of international students in fall 2026 declined by 9%, according to a survey of more than 800 institutions in the annual report, amid changing visa policies under the Trump administration and growing competition for scholars across the globe.

The annual Open Doors report provided a preliminary glimpse at enrolment during the current academic year. The slide was especially pronounced among graduate students, with universities reporting an estimated 15% decline in the fall. Undergraduate enrolment fell 3%.

Mirka Martel, head of research, evaluation and learning at the institute, said there have been several factors driving decreases in enrolment from foreign students. She noted visa policies as well as the rising cost of a degree in the US.

“One of the big changes we’re seeing is global competition,” she said in a call with reporters. “There are more countries actively investing in and recruiting international students. So as a result, this often means that there are more destination opportunities, and with rising costs and some of the other factors related to visas, I think that that’s also allowing international students to consider their options.”

See also: US wholesale inflation picks up to fastest pace since 2022

In the previous school year, undergraduate international enrolment dropped 0.3% but graduate enrolment fell 13%, the Open Doors report found.

Universities are now confronting the financial challenges posed by the decline in international students, who often pay full tuition to attend. The Open Doors survey found that personal and family funding accounted for the primary source of funding for nearly half of students.

For example, Pennsylvania State University said it faced a US$124 million budget gap for its US$2.2 billion budget, citing the drop in attendance from the cohort.

See also: Existing US home sales tumble to lowest level since 2010

“The financial pressures driving the shortfall are affecting universities nationwide, including declines in international, graduate and undergraduate student enrolment, and rising health insurance costs,” the university system said in a Nov 9 statement.

title: India to benefit from unwinding of AI trade, top official says
article:
(Nov 16): India’s markets stand to benefit from an artificial intelligence-led correction in global equities and an easing of global oil prices, the government’s chief economic advisor V Anantha Nageswaran said, in what would be a reversal of the first nine months of the year.

“India’s status as a non-AI play is definitely weighing positively on the Indian market sentiment and also drawing in foreign institutional investors in the near term,” Nageswaran told the Indian Express newspaper in an interview published Monday.

India has largely been sidelined during the AI investment boom of the past two years, and its stock market has performed accordingly, suggesting it will be well placed should investors pull back from markets that attracted a lot of technology-related investment.

India “would benefit if such a backlash were to occur in the AI financial ecosystem,” Nageswaran said, adding that “from the Indian perspective, it is net positive.”

The unwinding of the AI trade has helped Indian stocks outperform, with the MSCI India gauge rebounding 11% from a six-month low in October, adding more than US$400 billion in value and almost erasing this year’s losses. Overseas investors have bought a net US$8.5 billion of Indian shares so far in November, reducing year-to-date outflows to about US$22 billion.

See also: Alibaba unveils new flagship AI model in riposte to US rivals

Indian markets have also been buoyed by oil prices falling below US$100 a barrel, providing relief to oil-marketing companies and consumers as pump prices remain unchanged.

“The reason for optimism comes from oil companies doing well from June to August,” Nageswaran said, adding that high energy prices have so far not significantly hurt consumers’ disposable incomes or purchasing power.

title: Thai GDP growth rebounds as AI drives investments, exports
article:
(Nov 16): Thailand’s economic growth accelerated in the third quarter, with the artificial intelligence boom powering exports while masking persistent weakness in household spending and tourism.

Gross domestic product in the three months through September rose 2.9% from a year earlier, the National Economic and Social Development Council said Monday (Nov 16). That was below the 3.1% median estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

The pickup partly reflected a favourable comparison with a year earlier, when US tariffs and a border conflict with Cambodia disrupted trade. But it also showed the growing impact of the global tech investment cycle on Thailand, where electronics exports and private investment have surged.

The baht held gains of 0.1% versus the dollar as the local currency looked past the weaker-than-expected GDP.

Evidence of the tech sector’s impact was visible in an 11.8% jump in investment growth and an 18.3% surge in exports of goods and services.

See also: Why politicians love stimulus checks

But household consumption ticked up just 2.5% while government spending shrank 1.6%. That supports cautionary comments from the Bank of Thailand that gains from the AI boom have not reached all corners of the economy.

“The tech/AI cycle is improving economic momentum but the benefits remain concentrated among businesses and workers in related manufacturing and services sectors,” Standard Chartered plc economist Tim Leelahaphan said in a note. “Overall growth remains below potential.”

Nomura Holdings Inc economist Euben Paracuelles expects the central bank to keep its policy rate at 1% throughout 2027 as growth momentum fades in the final quarter. “The improvement wasn’t really strong and it’s driven by likely unsustainable factors such as government cash handouts,” he said.

See also: Losses from reselling homes in New Zealand hit 14-year high

Economic growth this year should be around 2.5%, the government said, giving a range of 2% to 3% for 2027. The current quarter’s growth may be softer because of a slowdown in private sector investment and a high base last year, NESDC secretary-general Danucha Pichayanan told reporters in Bangkok on Monday.

“Risks next year include a slowdown in global growth and trade, changing weather conditions affecting agricultural crops, relatively high household debt and a credit crunch for SMEs,” the council said.

The risks to Thailand’s agricultural sector from El Niño have been highlighted by crises in neighbouring countries, with climate change worsening wildfires in Indonesia and the Philippines seeing disappointing farm output.

It also remains to be seen whether AI demand will continue to surge, with the ouster of Jensen Huang as head of Nvidia Corp raising questions about the sector’s outlook.

But the overall economic data put Thailand ahead of the Philippines, which expanded 2.1% in the quarter. Thailand still trailed most regional peers, with Vietnam growing almost 10% and Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia all expanding more than 5%.

Over the past decade, annual growth above 3% has become unusual for Thailand, an ageing tiger economy constrained by high household debt and limited fiscal room. Using new methodology to better capture manufacturing data from various agencies, the government restated second-quarter growth to 2.4% from 1.9% and raised first-quarter growth to 3.1%.

“We have increased the sample size used in the calculation and adjusted the methodology to better reflect changes across industries,” Danucha said. “There are new businesses emerging, particularly in the services sector, which is an area we need to focus on.”

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The stronger performance comes during a period of unusual political stability. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul leads one of Thailand’s strongest governing coalitions in decades, giving his administration more room to pursue investment and economic policies even with a no-confidence vote looming next month and street protests simmering.

Thailand has also attracted a surge in investment tied to AI, data centres and advanced electronics while foreign investors have returned to its bonds and stocks.

The Bank of Thailand, which last month left its policy rate unchanged for a fourth straight meeting, raised its 2026 growth forecast to 2.4%, citing stronger-than-expected exports and AI-related investment. It has also flagged potential upside from revisions to manufacturing data.

The central bank has nevertheless maintained that monetary policy should remain accommodative to support an uneven recovery. Officials have highlighted a K-shaped expansion, with growth concentrated in sectors benefiting from the technology and AI investment cycle while other parts of the economy remain weak.

According to BOT’s recent monetary policy report, the expansion in AI-related shipments accounted for roughly 50%-67% of Thailand’s overall export growth. The top 1% of exporters, or about 69 firms, accounted for 83% of AI-related exports in the first eight months of 2026 and more than 70% of those firms were foreign-owned.

title: Copper sinks to four-month low on tech rout, China growth woes
article:
(Nov 16): Copper fell for a third day to the lowest in more than four months as a selloff in technology shares and weaker Chinese economic data darkened the demand outlook and sapped appetite for risk.

Futures on the London Metal Exchange dropped as much as 1.4% to the lowest level since July 8, extending a decline of five straight weekly losses. An upheaval in the artificial intelligence industry following the crisis at Nvidia Corp has weighed on sentiment. Expectations for further interest rate increases following hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve officials are adding pressure on the industrial metal, which is widely used in power infrastructure and data centres.

Technology-heavy stock benchmarks in South Korea and Taiwan tumbled more than 2.5% each on Monday (Nov 16), with Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic PBC’s expected listing set to test investor appetite for the AI trade this week.

Copper joined a broader decline in industrial metals after Chinese economic growth weakened across the board in October. Consumption and industrial production missed estimates while investment unexpectedly fell, signalling that Beijing’s latest stimulus measures have yet to feed through to the world’s biggest metals consumer.

Traders are also watching a major squeeze in tin on the LME, where spot prices have surged as dwindling inventories tighten immediate supplies of the metal, which is mainly used as solder in electronics. Falling exchange stockpiles have similarly fuelled steep backwardation in copper and aluminium in recent months, a sign that near-term supplies are tight.

See also: China’s iron ore buying clout makes each deal a market event

Copper was down 1.2% at US$13,240 a tonne as of 11.55am in Shanghai. Aluminium fell 0.7% to US$2,989.50 while tin was down 1.7% to $45,915 a tonne.

title: Goldman Sachs predicts ‘sizeable surplus’ for oil market in 2027
article:
(Nov 16): The oil market faces a “sizeable surplus” next year that’ll drag prices lower even as supply risks remain, Goldman Sachs Group Inc said.

Crude production minus so-called end-use demand will reach two million barrels a day in 2027, despite accounting for supply disruptions half that size, analysts including Daan Struyven said in a Nov 15 note outlining their base case. Brent futures are expected to average US$88 a barrel next year, easing to US$78 by the year-end “as the risk premium gradually normalises,” they said.

The worldwide crude market has been rocked this year by the US-Iran war, which initially choked off regional production before suppliers tapped alternative export routes and restored flows through the Strait of Hormuz. The Paris-based International Energy Agency (IEA) said last week that the global oil market is set to swing to a surplus for the first time since the conflict began.

“For 2027, we again expect a contest between high supply disruption risk and increasing market adaptation,” they said. “Under our base case, Mideast supply rises above its 2025 average on ongoing adaptation through ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline additions, while supply growth elsewhere stalls.”

China — typically the world’s largest crude importer — is unlikely to prop up prices, with “persistent weakness” in road-fuel usage to scar demand by 400,000 barrels a day, according to the Goldman analysts. All in, “we estimate that China’s total oil demand peaked in 2025,” they added.

Brent traded below US$95 a barrel on Monday after dropping more than 1%. The benchmark peaked this year above US$126 a barrel in April, hitting the highest intraday price since 2022. Year-to-date, it’s averaged about US$91.

See also: The oil market is brimming with crude despite tanker attacks

title: Alibaba unveils new flagship AI model in riposte to US rivals
article:
(Nov 16): Alibaba Group Holding Ltd launched a new flagship AI model, claiming performance that rivals Anthropic PBC and OpenAI in China’s latest challenge to US leaders.

The e-commerce giant-turned-AI player said its Qwen4-Max model scored near the top of coding benchmarks, outperforming Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 as well as homegrown rival Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro. Alibaba did not make the model open weight, which would allow users to download and customize it, but said it would make smaller versions of the series available soon.

Chinese firms including Alibaba, Moonshot and DeepSeek are challenging US dominance in artificial intelligence, unveiling a succession of new models with rapid improvements in coding and reasoning. Monday’s release adds to a flurry of recent Chinese launches, including Tencent’s Hunyuan 4 and Moonshot’s Kimi K3.1 Pro.

Alibaba’s Qwen series is so far the most downloaded open-weight model family in the world following an ambitious push into the technology spearheaded by chief executive officer Eddie Wu. The company is building a full AI ecosystem, from models to AI chips.

The CEO said in September that Alibaba’s T-Head chipmaking unit, which recently filed for an IPO in Hong Kong, would roll out China’s most powerful AI chips domestically.

The Hangzhou, China-headquartered firm has made attaining artificial general intelligence, or AGI, its primary goal. It is also rapidly expanding its computing power, with Wu setting a target of building 20 gigawatts of data centre capacity globally by 2032.

See also: Nvidia’s CEO search draws fire with Bessent’s ‘shake-up’ call

The firm introduced upgraded security measures in its latest model, following a series of alarming incidents that have raised concerns over the cybersecurity risks of open-weight models. That follows similar moves from Tencent and Moonshot.

title: SK Hynix plans chip testing hub to boost smaller Korean players
article:
(Nov 16): SK Hynix Inc plans to open a semiconductor testing facility next year in partnership with the Korean government, angling to boost the global competitiveness of the country’s smaller chip equipment makers.

The 874.6 billion won (US$654 million) facility is being built inside the sprawling Yongin Semiconductor Cluster, which is under construction south of Seoul, SK Hynix said in a statement on Monday. The Trinity Fab facility will open in May with equipment that small and medium-sized suppliers can use to conduct final performance and yield validation before their products are deployed in commercial chipmaking lines, it said.

SK Hynix and homegrown rival Samsung Electronics Co have enjoyed an unprecedented run-up in prices because of a chip scarcity that’s squeezed industries from autos to smartphones. The company is working with the Korean government to eliminate a critical hurdle in the country’s supply chain that has required access to expensive manufacturing infrastructure.

The facility is being jointly financed by SK Hynix, the central government and local authorities, the company said. It will house about 50 pieces of equipment for lithography, etching, deposition, cleaning and measurement, allowing suppliers to test products on 12-inch wafers under conditions resembling those of commercial chip production.

The initiative aims to address a longstanding bottleneck for Korea’s semiconductor supply chain. Smaller materials and equipment makers often face steep costs and lengthy delays in securing access to production-scale testing facilities, making it difficult to demonstrate that their technologies meet the stringent performance and yield requirements of advanced chip manufacturing.

See also: Wingtech to challenge Dutch Court’s interim order on Nexperia

Unlike conventional research laboratories and pilot lines, Trinity Fab will be the world’s first open-access testing facility specifically designed to validate commercial manufacturing readiness for mass production, according to SK Hynix. An independent nonprofit foundation will operate the center to safeguard participants’ intellectual property.

In August, SK Hynix said it would spend US$38 billion to expand its local chipmaking facilities, including a new DRAM manufacturing facility in Yongin and a NAND fabrication plant in Cheongju. The move, covering both dynamic memory for the lowest latency and solid-state storage for fast access to greater quantities of data, is in response to growing demand for memory in the AI era, the company said at the time.

title: Indonesia’s Prabowo apologizes to Singapore, Malaysia for haze
article:
(Nov 16): Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto apologised to Singapore and Malaysia for the transboundary haze that blanketed parts of Southeast Asia in recent months.

He “apologised on behalf of the Indonesian government and people for the impact of the forest and land fires on the people of Singapore and Malaysia,” according to a Nov 15 statement. The country is preparing to “establish new institutions and implement various programmes to strengthen forest fire prevention in the future,” the statement added.

Acrid haze from Indonesian forest fires spurred poor air quality alerts across the region and disrupted palm harvests as a powerful El Niño brought abnormally hot and dry conditions, prompting Singapore and Jakarta to form a joint taskforce to tackle such blazes.

Separately, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on Sunday called for a regional haze platform to coordinate and share information on companies behind the haze, the Straits Times reported.

title: Exceptional companies named winners of the 2026 regional Golden Bull award amid economic headwinds
article:
In a challenging economic climate marked by rising costs and global trade uncertainty, 21 exceptional companies have emerged victorious at the 2026 Regional Golden Bull Award organised by Business Media International. These winning enterprises have demonstrated remarkable resilience and innovation, standing out as beacons of success in a highly competitive landscape.

The current economic landscape has presented unprecedented hurdles. Recent market surveys reveal that 41% of SMEs expect business conditions to worsen in the near term. In the past year, only 43% of Singaporean businesses reported growth—a notable decline as global trade uncertainties and rising operational costs take their toll.

The primary challenges stifling SME expansion include high transformation and digitalization costs, which impact 47% of businesses. Additionally, 46% of SMEs cite severe financing barriers driven by high interest rates, while 36% continue to struggle with persistent manpower and skills shortages.

Amidst this economic crisis, the 21 winners of the 2026 Golden Bull Award have successfully navigated these pain points through agile business models, strategic digital adoption, and outstanding leadership. Winning this prestigious award—widely recognized as the ultimate emblem of success—provides a critical competitive advantage. The accolade allows these SMEs to cut through market noise, instantly elevating their brand credibility to attract top talent and overcome financing barriers. Winners gain access to exclusive global brand exposure, high-level networking opportunities, and invitations to international trade and investment missions, giving them the exact tools needed to scale beyond local borders.

Datuk William Ng, Chairman of the Golden Bull Award, commended the winning cohort for their outstanding achievements in such a demanding environment.

"The 21 companies honored today represent the absolute best of Singapore's entrepreneurial spirit," said Datuk William Ng. "While many businesses are currently weighed down by manpower shortages and soaring operational costs, these winners have chosen to innovate and push forward. The Golden Bull Award is not just a trophy; it is a testament to their resilience and a platform that provides the visibility and network necessary to turn today's economic challenges into tomorrow's market leadership."

As the industry benchmark for business excellence, the Golden Bull Award continues its stringent evaluation process to ensure that only the most resilient and forward-thinking enterprises take home the statuette. The 2026 winners have proven that with the right strategies, SMEs can not only survive but thrive and command the market during economic downturns.

Since its founding in 2003, the Golden Bull Award has stood as a benchmark of SME excellence across Asia. With expansion into new Asia Pacific markets on the horizon for 2026, it continues to spotlight the region’s most inspiring business stories.
